reasons: Correctly classified as a deviation: Article IV fixes a 36-month Initial Period and the only termination rights run to Licensor (breach) or are mutual/insolvency/change-of-control; there is no Licensee convenience exit, which fails even the fallback and sits in walk-away territory for a multi-year term.

The redline is additive and minimal: it leaves the existing term language untouched and inserts a new Section IV granting Licensee a 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no early-termination penalty, tracking the model language and preferred position. No Vendor convenience right exists, so no deletion was required.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, cites the playbook position and offers the 60-day fallback.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') reflects the absence of such a right in the original clause — which is the very basis of the finding — and not a defect in the proposed edit; the inserted paragraph plainly grants Licensee a 30-day convenience termination.
